personalTemplates.rule: Remote personal templates require an authenticated owner. Client fallback may expose locally owned templates but must not label them synced or remote.

candidateDeploymentGate.rule: The current cloud main runtime predates the branch endpoint. Candidate deployment must expose the exact typed simc-options-v1 response before this route can be called production-ready; the frontend must not replace a missing or malformed payload with local races, scenarios, durations or preparation rules.

trustRules: Target profession icons, race, template names, validation statuses, missing-item bullets, spinner state, task state and any result-like copy are placeholders and never runtime facts.

The target defines ten stable first-level regions, six visible specialization selector positions, two template slots, three scenario positions, one duration control, four buff-rule rows, six summary rows, five blocker rows, two primary actions and one footer utility action.

Profession or specialization choices come only from the verified builds.home class/spec mapping. Six positions are a visible viewport over the real collection and cannot imply only six supported specializations.

Supported races, scenarios, scenario-owned durations and preparation rules come only from the typed simulator.simcOptions payload. A missing, fallback or malformed simc-options-v1 response blocks the route and must not be replaced by app-owned defaults.
Remote personal templates require an authenticated owner. A local template remains explicitly local or stale and cannot be presented as synchronized source evidence.

Talent and gear empty states keep their target slots and block confirmation. Gear selection may use the canonical equipment-detail handoff or a typed personal gear template only when its metadata contains a valid canonical selectionIntent; the page must not synthesize a template or gear fact from display fields or raw JSON alone.

The target's four buff rows remain visible, but the current request contract does not accept user-managed buff overrides. They are read-only rule or unavailable rows until a typed backend contract exists.
Changing specialization, race, scenario (including its backend-owned duration), talent template or gear source invalidates any prior confirmation.

Confirmation first requires a parseable gear snapshot, then a non-fallback websim.gearStatSnapshots result whose statStatus is not blocked, then simulator.analyze with confirmOnly=true and explicit agent.validation.passed=true.
confirmOnly validation does not execute SimC, save a task or authorize any DPS claim. No result preview, DPS, rank or completion state may be fabricated before a real task completes.
Final submission re-reads simulator.tasks, blocks on an active task or transport fallback, sends confirmOnly=false and saveTask=true, and only succeeds when the backend returns a taskId.

Loading, empty, stale, blocked and error states retain all ten target regions; state copy inhabits the owned region instead of mounting generic RouteStatePanel, WowPanel, TemplateLibrary or EvidenceLedger compositions.

mappings.runtime: AppShell pushed-route surface and PageFrame simc-submit variant
back navigation, fixed SimC 提交 title and real task-record navigation
six-position visible selector viewport over verified specializations plus the supported race selector
selected real local or remote talent template, or a stable empty blocked slot
selected canonical equipment-detail handoff or real local/remote gear template with valid selectionIntent metadata, or a stable empty blocked slot
real scenario options, one scenario-owned read-only duration value and four read-only buff-rule positions
six derived selection and readiness rows from current specialization, race, scenario, duration and template state
five stable blocker positions derived from template presence, active tasks, gear stats and backend validation
real confirmation state, confirm-only action, final submit action and returned taskId state
truth boundary notice and navigation to current task rules or records

stateContract.loading: mount all ten regions with stable selector, template, configuration, summary, blocker and action positions
stateContract.empty: retain both template panels as empty blocked slots and derive missing-template blockers without inventing templates
stateContract.stale: retain local templates with explicit local or stale source state and require fresh backend confirmation
stateContract.confirming: retain geometry, disable duplicate actions and expose the gear-stats then confirm-only validation stage
stateContract.ready: enable final submit only after explicit validation.passed and retain the exact confirmed request snapshot
stateContract.blocked: retain all regions and show real parse, stats, validation or active-task blockers
stateContract.submitting: retain geometry, re-check active tasks and disable duplicate final submission
stateContract.submitted: show only the returned taskId and task navigation; do not synthesize result values
stateContract.error: retain all regions and allow deterministic retry after transport or missing-taskId failure
